qs.q: A 45-year-old woman with autoimmune hepatitis is monitored for disease progression. Which pharmacokinetic property of hepatic coagulation factors makes prothrombin time a sensitive marker for both acute and chronic liver injury?
o: Rapid degradation by the renal system
High volume of distribution in adipose tissue
Short half-life in the systemic circulation
Extensive binding to plasma albumin carriers
qs.e: The short half-life of hepatic coagulation factors allows prothrombin time to quickly detect acute synthetic failure. They are primarily degraded via proteolysis rather than renal elimination.

qs.q: Which diagnostic autoantibodies are classically associated with the workup of autoimmune hepatitis?
o: Anti-nuclear antibodies and smooth muscle antibodies
Anti-double stranded DNA and Smith antibodies
Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide and rheumatoid factor
qs.e: Autoimmune hepatitis is investigated using anti-nuclear antibodies (ANA), smooth muscle antibodies (SMA), anti-SLA, and LKM antibodies, along with hyperglobulinemia. Anti-mitochondrial antibodies are typical of primary biliary cholangitis.

qs.q: What is the first-line pharmacological treatment approach specifically indicated for autoimmune hepatitis?
qs.e: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is treated with steroids and azathioprine. Interferons are used for viral hepatitis, and thiamine with alcohol cessation is used for alcoholic liver disease.
